title: Our Beliefs and Values
author: Dn Yonnas
summary: The foundational beliefs and values of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church. Anchored in the Orthodox Creed of the holy councils, it walks through the confession of one God in three Persons, the nature of man, sin and salvation, the Person of the Lord Jesus Christ, the Holy Spirit, the Church and her sacraments, the Kingdom of God, the Christian family, and eternity — each teaching rooted in Holy Scripture.

sections.h2: Introduction: Servants' Lessons in the Faith

sections.p: This is a catechetical guide to what the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church believes, confesses, and treasures, that those who labor in the Lord's vineyard might know it clearly. The aim is not novelty but faithfulness: to hand on the deposit of faith "once for all delivered to the saints" (Jude 1:3), as it has been received and guarded by the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church within the wider communion of the Oriental Orthodox Churches. What follows is an in-depth presentation of that teaching, ordered from the confession of God Himself, through His works of creation and redemption, to the life of the Church and the hope of the age to come.

The word Tewahedo means "made one" or "unified," and it expresses the very heart of the Church's confession of Christ: that in the Incarnation the divine and human were perfectly united in the one Person of God the Word, without division, without confusion, without change, and without separation. This single word both names the Church and summarizes her unshakable faith.

The Church's faith is summed up in the Creed proclaimed by the holy Fathers at the Ecumenical Councils of Nicaea (325) and Constantinople (381) and confirmed at Ephesus (431). It is recited as the common confession of all the faithful, the standard against which every teaching is measured. The lessons open with this Creed because all other beliefs flow from it and are governed by it.

sections.quote: We believe in one God, God the Father the Pantocrator who created heaven and earth, and all things seen and unseen. We believe in one Lord Jesus Christ, the Only-Begotten Son of God, begotten of the Father before all ages; Light of Light, true God of true God, begotten not created, of one essence with the Father, by whom all things were made; Who for us men and for our salvation came down from heaven, and was incarnate of the Holy Spirit and the Virgin Mary and became Man. And He was crucified for us under Pontius Pilate, suffered and was buried. And on the third day He rose from the dead,

according to the scriptures, ascended to the heavens; He sits at the right hand of His Father, and He is coming again in His glory to judge the living and the dead, Whose kingdom shall have no end. Yes, we believe in the Holy Spirit, the Lord, the Life-Giver, Who proceeds from the Father, Who with the Father and the Son is worshipped and glorified, who spoke by the prophets. And in one, holy, catholic and apostolic church. We confess one baptism for the remission of sins. We look for the resurrection of the dead, and the life of the coming age. Amen.

sections.p: Several confessions in the Creed are decisive for the Orthodox faith. The Son is "begotten not created, of one essence with the Father," against every teaching that would make Him a creature. He "became Man" truly and fully, not in appearance only. And the Holy Spirit "proceeds from the Father" alone, as the Lord Himself taught (John 15:26); the Church confesses this single procession and does not add "and the Son" to the Creed, keeping the faith exactly as the Fathers handed it down. The Spirit is nonetheless "with the Father and the Son worshipped and glorified," for the three Persons share one undivided honor and one Godhead.

God is the completely holy and sovereign Creator and Sustainer of the universe. He alone is uncreated, eternal, almighty (Pantocrator), and the source of all that exists, both the things seen and the things unseen. Nothing is His equal, and nothing endures apart from His will, for He both made all things and continually upholds them in being.

This one God exists in three Persons: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. The three Persons are co-equal and co-eternal, yet truly distinct from one another. The Church confesses one essence (one being, one Godhead) in three Persons (three hypostases): not three gods, and not one Person wearing three names, but the one God who is eternally Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. The Father is unbegotten; the Son is eternally begotten of the Father; the Holy Spirit eternally proceeds from the Father. They are inseparable in essence, will, power, and glory, distinct only in their personal properties.

Because God is holy and sovereign, He is worthy of all worship, trust, and obedience. To know Him rightly is the beginning of all true life, and to confess Him as Trinity is the foundation of the whole faith.

list: 1 Samuel 2:2 - There is none holy like the Lord
1 Chronicles 29:11-12 - Greatness, power, and sovereignty belong to God
Isaiah 6:3 - Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts
Isaiah 46:10 - He declares the end from the beginning
Matthew 28:19 - Baptizing in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit
2 Corinthians 13:14 - The grace, love, and fellowship of the Holy Trinity

sections.p: God created man in His own image. Out of all of creation, man is set apart as God's special image-bearer. This is the ground of every person's inherent worth and dignity, and also of a special responsibility: because man bears the image of God, every human life is precious, and man is accountable to live in a way that reflects his Maker.

Man was created with a body fashioned from the earth and a living soul breathed into him by God Himself (Genesis 2:7). He was made not for himself alone but for communion: he was created to know God and to worship God. The purpose of human existence, therefore, is not found in any earthly thing but in the knowledge, love, and worship of the One whose image he bears. To live for this end is to live truly as man; to turn from it is to fall short of what man was made to be.

list: Genesis 1:26 - Let Us make man in Our image, after Our likeness
Genesis 2:7 - God formed man and breathed into him the breath of life
Isaiah 43:7 - Everyone called by My name, whom I created for My glory

sections.p: Through the disobedience of Adam and Eve, sin entered the world and broke God's good creation. What God had made very good was wounded by the transgression of the first parents, and the consequences of that fall did not remain contained: the effects of sin permeate all of creation, including every person born into the world.

Sin is not merely the breaking of a rule; it is a rupture of relationship and a corruption of the human person. Sin separates a person from God, from their own true self, and from others. The harmony for which man was created, communion with God, integrity within, and love toward neighbor, is fractured by sin. Because of sin, man stands guilty before God, deserves punishment, and is in himself incapable of loving, worshipping, or cherishing God as he ought. The human will is bound, and the heart is turned away from its true end.

This sober diagnosis is essential, for it shows why man cannot save himself and why salvation must come from God. To understand the gravity of sin is to understand the greatness of the grace that meets it.

list: Genesis 3 - The disobedience of Adam and Eve and its consequences
Psalm 51:5 - In sin did my mother conceive me
Romans 3:23 - All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God
Romans 5:12 - Through one man sin entered the world
Romans 6:23 - The wages of sin is death
Ephesians 2:1-3 - Dead in trespasses and sins

sections.p: The sinful state in which man finds himself cannot be overcome by any of his own efforts. No amount of human striving, merit, or self-improvement can heal the breach that sin has opened or cleanse the guilt it has incurred. Salvation must therefore be received, not achieved.

God, according to His grace, offers salvation to man as a free gift. This gift is obtained through faith in the saving work of Jesus Christ on the Cross. Those in whom the work of Christ becomes effective are born again: they are given a new heart, a heart that loves God, hates sin, and desires to live an obedient life. Salvation is thus not only the forgiveness of past sins but the gift of a transformed life, a new creation made alive in Christ.

While salvation is by grace and received through faith, the Orthodox Tewahedo Church teaches that this saving faith is living and is worked out in the life of the Church. The lessons name the essentials through which God's saving grace is communicated and lived out: faith, baptism, the sacraments of the Church, and good works. Faith opens the door; baptism unites the believer to the death and resurrection of Christ; the sacraments nourish and renew the new life; and good works are the fruit and evidence of a heart genuinely made new. These are not human achievements that earn salvation, but the means by which the gift of God is received, kept, and brought to maturity.

list: Faith - trusting in the work of Jesus Christ
Baptism - new birth and union with Christ
Sacraments of the Church - the ongoing nourishment of grace
Good works - the living fruit of a renewed heart
John 3:16-18 - God so loved the world that He gave His only Son
2 Corinthians 5:17 - If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation
Ephesians 2:4-10 - By grace you have been saved through faith, for good works

sections.p: Jesus Christ is the Son of God, the Only-Begotten of the Father, begotten before all ages. He is both fully God and fully man. In the Incarnation, the eternal Word who is true God of true God came down from heaven and was incarnate of the Holy Spirit and the Virgin Mary, taking to Himself a complete and real humanity, body and rational soul, without ceasing to be what He eternally is.

The Church confesses the mystery of this union in her very name, Tewahedo, "made one." In Christ, divinity and humanity are united in one Person and one incarnate nature of God the Word, without mixture, without confusion, without change, without alteration, and without separation. His Godhead never departed from His manhood for a single moment, not on the Cross, not in the tomb. He is not divided into two, nor is His humanity swallowed up and lost in His divinity; He is one Christ, one Lord, perfect in Godhead and perfect in manhood.

This same Lord Jesus lived a perfect, sinless life, and died upon the Cross as the sacrifice for the sins of the whole world. He truly suffered, was crucified under Pontius Pilate, and was buried. On the third day He rose bodily from the grave, displaying His victory over sin, Satan, and death. He ascended into the heavens and sits at the right hand of the Father. And He will one day return in glory to earth, to judge the living and the dead and to reign as King, and of His Kingdom there shall be no end.

list: Isaiah 42:1 - Behold My servant, whom I uphold, My chosen
John 1:1-5 - In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was God
John 10:30 - I and the Father are one
John 14:6 - I am the way, the truth, and the life
Romans 6:4 - Raised from the dead by the glory of the Father
Colossians 1:19-20 - In Him all the fullness of God was pleased to dwell

sections.p: The Holy Spirit is the third Person of the Holy Trinity, the Lord, the Life-Giver, who proceeds from the Father and is, together with the Father and the Son, worshipped and glorified. He is fully God, co-equal and co-eternal with the Father and the Son, sharing the one undivided Godhead.

It is the Holy Spirit who spoke by the prophets and who inspired the Holy Scriptures, so that the written Word of God is His own breath. The same Spirit illuminates the Word of God, opening the minds of the faithful to understand it, and convicts people of sin, awakening the conscience and drawing the heart to repentance. He empowers believers to live the life God has called them to, sanctifying them and conforming them to Christ.

By the Holy Spirit, believers receive spiritual gifts. These gifts are not given for self-glory but for service: they are to be used to build up and serve the local parish church and the whole Body of Christ. The fruit of the Spirit, love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control, marks the life of those who walk in Him.

list: John 14:26 - The Helper, the Holy Spirit, will teach you all things
John 16:7-15 - He will convict the world and guide you into all truth
Romans 8:26 - The Spirit helps us in our weakness
Romans 12:6-8 - Gifts that differ according to grace given to us
Galatians 5:22-25 - The fruit of the Spirit

sections.p: The Church is one, holy, catholic, and apostolic, as the Creed confesses. In its local expression, a church is a community of baptized believers, gathered in a particular place, committed to one another and to the mission of God. They gather regularly under recognizable leadership, practice the sacraments of the Church, and live and function as a team and a family bound together in Christ.

The Church is not a mere association of like-minded people but the household of God, "the pillar and ground of the truth" (1 Timothy 3:15). Within her, ordered leadership is established, the priesthood and the offices of the Church, so that the flock may be shepherded, taught, and led in good order. The faithful are called not to isolated belief but to a shared life of mutual love, encouragement, accountability, and worship, stirring one another up to love and good works and not neglecting to gather together.

list: 1 Timothy 3:15 - The church of the living God, pillar and ground of the truth
Titus 1:5-9 - The appointment and qualifications of church leaders
Hebrews 10:24-25 - Not neglecting to meet together, but encouraging one another

sections.p: The Church practices baptism, which is among the first acts of obedience for a follower of Jesus Christ. Baptism marks and demonstrates the person's new life in Christ: in it the old life of sin is buried and a new life is begun. The Orthodox Tewahedo Church administers baptism by immersion, by which the believer is united to the death and resurrection of the Lord and washed for the remission of sins, as the Creed confesses: "We confess one baptism for the remission of sins."

Baptism is therefore far more than an outward symbol; it is the doorway into the new birth and into the communion of the Church. In the waters of baptism the believer puts on Christ and is born again of water and the Spirit.

list: Mark 16:16 - Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved
Acts 2:38 - Repent and be baptized for the forgiveness of your sins

sections.p: The Church practices Holy Communion. In the Eucharist the faithful partake of the bread and the wine, set apart in remembrance of the saving work of Jesus Christ upon the Cross: the bread is His body, broken for us, and the wine is His blood, shed for us. In the Lord's own words, "unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink His blood, you have no life in you" (John 6:53). Through this holy mystery, established by Christ Himself at the Last Supper, the believer is joined to Him and receives the life He gives, proclaiming the Lord's death until He comes.

list: John 6:53-57 - Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood has eternal life
1 Corinthians 11:23-26 - This is My body; this cup is the new covenant in My blood

sections.p: The Kingdom of God is His rule, His reign, and His authority. This Kingdom is already present in the world, breaking in through the work of Christ and the life of His Church, yet it is not fully expressed; it awaits its consummation. The faithful live in the tension of the Kingdom that has come and the Kingdom that is still to come in fullness.

When a person is born again, that person's citizenship is, in essence, transferred from the kingdom of darkness into the Kingdom of God. The believer is no longer ruled by sin and the powers of darkness but is brought under the loving reign of God. And there is a sure hope: one day God's rule, reign, and authority will be perfectly expressed, when His will is done "on earth as it is in heaven," and every knee shall bow before the King of glory.

list: Psalm 103:19 - The Lord has established His throne, and His kingdom rules over all
Luke 1:32-33 - He will reign forever, and of His kingdom there will be no end
John 3:5-7 - Unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God

sections.p: Marriage is a covenantal relationship instituted by God Himself, between one man and one woman, and it provides the foundation for the family. From the beginning God made them male and female, and what God has joined together, no one is to separate (Matthew 19:6). Marriage is therefore not a mere human contract but a sacred covenant, an image of the faithful, self-giving love between Christ and His Church (Ephesians 5:22-33).

Within this teaching, sexual intimacy is to be practiced only within a lifelong, covenantal, monogamous, and heterosexual marriage. The home built upon such a marriage is meant to be a place of holiness, the first school of faith and love, where children are raised in the knowledge and worship of God and the values of the Church are handed on to the next generation.

list: Genesis 2:23-24 - A man shall hold fast to his wife, and they shall become one flesh
Matthew 19:6 - What God has joined together, let no one separate
1 Corinthians 6:9-20 - Glorify God in your body
Ephesians 5:22-33 - Marriage as the image of Christ and the Church

sections.p: Man was created to exist forever; the soul is immortal, and the dead shall be raised. The faith looks for "the resurrection of the dead, and the life of the coming age." Eternity is therefore not an abstract idea but the real and final destiny of every human person, determined by their relationship to Jesus Christ.

Those who are in Christ will spend eternity in the new heavens and the new earth, in new and unending life, under the rule and reign of the good King Jesus Christ, forever. This is the believer's blessed hope: not merely the absence of death, but everlasting communion with God in a renewed creation. By contrast, those who reject Jesus will experience the wrath of God and spend eternity separated from God in hell. The weight of this truth is itself a summons to faith, repentance, and perseverance, that none may be lost but all may come to the King who is good.

list: Matthew 25:41-46 - The eternal separation of the righteous and the unrighteous
2 Corinthians 5:21 - That in Him we might become the righteousness of God
1 John 5:11-12 - Whoever has the Son has life

sections.h2: Conclusion: Glory Be to the Holy Trinity

sections.p: From the confession of the one God in three Persons to the hope of eternal life, these beliefs and values form a single, coherent witness to the faith of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church. They begin and end in the worship of God: the Father who created, the Son who redeemed, and the Holy Spirit who sanctifies and gives life. To hold this faith is to know God, to be united to Christ in His Church and sacraments, to live a life made new by grace and bearing the fruit of good works, and to await with confident hope the coming Kingdom of our Lord.

sections.quote: Glory be to the Holy Trinity, The Father, The Son, and The Holy Spirit, ONE GOD. Amen!
